One model, one pass — no way to check the work
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
A single confident pass leaves no seam to check what evidence was used. Jobs, arrows, and shared state make the same work checkable at every step, not just at the end.
 
Decision: run the six-condition test (slide 8) before scaling risky AI work — then start with a manual first rep, not a tooling purchase.

4
 
 
One active framing — not a settled progression
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
Prompt engineering is about wording, context engineering about information, graph engineering about how the work is designed — three levers, not an agreed sequence.
 
Take the mechanics (design the work, not just the prompt) without adopting the trend-cycle framing wholesale.

5
 
 
The vocabulary: jobs, arrows, and one shared record
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
A job is one step with one owner and one output. An arrow says what has to happen before what. State is the shared record every job reads and writes. That's the entire vocabulary — nothing more exotic is required to start.
 
This is the whole mental model. Everything else in this deck is this vocabulary applied to a real decision.
Designing AI Workflows That Can Be Trusted
5 / 14
Slide 6
1/27/13
6
 
 
Same report format — different shape of work behind it
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
A single chat and a structured graph can both hand back a report. Only one of them lets you see which claims were checked, by whom, before you trust the answer.
 
Ask of any AI-produced recommendation: can I see the work behind it, or only the output?
Designing AI Workflows That Can Be Trusted
6 / 14
Slide 7
1/27/13
7
 
 
Don't confuse a knowledge graph with an agent graph
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
A knowledge graph maps what your data means — customers, products, relationships. An agent graph maps how work should move, get checked, and get approved. This deck is about the second one.
 
Buying or building a knowledge graph does not give you a checkable AI workflow — they solve different problems.
Designing AI Workflows That Can Be Trusted
7 / 14
Slide 8
1/27/13
8
 
 
The qualifying test: when a graph earns its place
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
Multiple steps, multiple sources, parallel paths, real checks, real risk, required approvals — if none of these are true for a workflow, a graph is overhead, not sophistication.
 
Run every candidate workflow through this test before reaching for any framework. Most AI work still doesn't need one.

9
 
 
Worked example: AI bookkeeping for Shopify?
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
Three parallel researchers cover customer pain, competitors, and distribution. A skeptic attacks the findings. A merge step turns survivors into a one-page recommendation. A human picks the next move.
 
The messy one-shot chat becomes a workflow you can actually inspect, challenge, and reuse on the next decision.

10
 
 
The pattern underneath: the Diamond
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
Planner fans out to parallel researchers, a skeptic checks their findings, then merge and human approval close the loop. This is the one shape worth learning first — every other pattern is a variation on it.
 
Learn this one diagram before anything else. It generalizes to support, content, and code work (next slide).
Designing AI Workflows That Can Be Trusted
10 / 14
Slide 11
1/27/13
11
 
 
Three ready-made pipelines you can steal
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
Support, content, and code workflows all follow the same rule: the checker is never the same role as the writer. That one constraint is what makes each pipeline trustworthy enough to run unattended.
 
Pick the lane closest to your own work and copy the structure — not the specific steps — into your first graph.
Designing AI Workflows That Can Be Trusted

Slide 12

12
 
 
Three levels of implementation — start manual
 
 
 
BUSINESS IMPLICATION
Manual whiteboard lanes prove the shape works with no code at all. File trails make the run reusable. Real orchestration tooling only pays off after that — earn the tooling, don't start with it.
 
Do not buy or install anything before finishing Level 1 by hand at least once.
